profiles._comment_archetypes: EVERY ARCHETYPE BELOW CARRIES ITS OWN `opening_loadout`, `starting_units`, `starting_knowledge_tags` AND `inventory` - what one kind of people opens with; the human seat always takes the first archetype, roster ids are handed out in archetype order, and placement lays the archetypes down in the same order, each at its own `min_separation` from every start already placed (a minor people fills the gaps the majors leave). `default_count` is the pin on how many a world gets when nobody picked (null = derive on New Game, none on an unattended boot). The rest of this note describes the opening_loadout block, which each archetype repeats with its own values. THE TURN-ONE OUTFITTING WINDOW, AND THE ONLY SOURCE OF OPENING GEAR AND MATERIAL. A spawning band owns NOTHING - equipment.json ships `start_stock_fraction: 0.0` and no material declares a start stock any more - so the player composes the opening loadout after seeing the generated map, and anything unspent when the first turn advances is forfeited. ONE BUDGET, AND IT IS NOT CONFIGURED HERE: the band's CARRY, its working-age value x expedition_config.json carry.per_worker_carry (about 17.85 x 7.0 = 125 on the shipped 30-person band), and what a band carries includes its food. The spawned larder is FIXED - there is nowhere to leave it - so it counts against the carry, and kits and materials are spent from what it leaves (about 125 - 78 = 47 on the shipped band) in one load currency - a kit weighs the items it expands to x carry.item_carry_weight, a material unit weighs carry.material_carry_weight. A retuned band size, working share, larder or pack moves the budget with no edit here. `pickable_materials` is the pick list the client draws, in the order it draws them; a material absent from it cannot be bought at any price, which is how the three luxury crops and `hurdles` stay off a list nobody would spend on. `material_defaults` and `kit_defaults` are the DEFAULT OUTFIT the sim applies to the opening band on the world-build pass, after the meal it eats there, so it is fitted to the same room the card shows - the allocation the window opens on, which the player is free to revise - and must name only pickable materials and roster kits that carry something. There is no sum check: the budget is the band's own carry, which does not exist at load, so the defaults are FITTED (materials cut before kits, each proportional, floored, remainder unspent) to whatever budget the band turned out to have, with a warn on the opening band when it binds. The shipped default is ONE KIT PER HAND on the shipped band's 17 hands - Stalking 5 / Trapping 5 / Harvesting 7 (10 + 10 + 7 = 27 of load) - and bone 2 / fibre 12 / hide 6 (20), a load of 47 against the about 47.2 the card shows, so it FITS WHOLE. One per hand because a split's kits are the splinter's proportional share (floor(kits x asked / whole hands)): a band with a kit per hand hands an untouched splinter a kit per worker. A splinter is not outfitted from these defaults - its default is that share in its parent's mix, then its food share, then materials. Every picked unit arrives at the MIDDLE of the band table on every axis it declares (OPENING_MATERIAL_READING): what the band scavenged before setting out is unremarkable.
